default.name: Default Example
default.description: A basic scenario with 4 processes to get started

convoy.name: Convoy Effect Demonstration
convoy.description: Shows the convoy effect where short processes wait for a long process in FCFS

expectedBehavior.fcfs: Poor performance - short processes wait for long process
expectedBehavior.sjf: Better - but P1 starts first and blocks others
expectedBehavior.srtf: Best - preempts P1 for shorter processes
expectedBehavior.rr: Fair - all processes get CPU time regularly

teachingPoints: Average waiting time very high in FCFS

starvation.name: Priority Starvation
starvation.description: Demonstrates how low priority processes can starve in priority scheduling

expectedBehavior.priority: P3 (priority 2) executes last, waits long time

teachingPoints: MLFQ handles this better than simple priority

mixed.name: Mixed Workload
mixed.description: Mix of short, medium, and long processes with varying priorities
teachingPoints: Different algorithms optimize for different metrics

iobound.name: I/O Bound Processes
iobound.description: Short CPU bursts simulating I/O bound processes

expectedBehavior.priority: High priority (0) processes get quick response
expectedBehavior.mlfq: Processes stay in high priority queues

teachingPoints: I/O bound processes have short CPU bursts
Round Robin works well for interactive processes
MLFQ naturally prioritizes I/O bound processes

cpubound.name: CPU Bound Processes
cpubound.description: Long CPU bursts simulating CPU intensive processes

expectedBehavior.rr: High context switching overhead for little benefit

teachingPoints: CPU bound processes have long bursts
Large quantum or non-preemptive better here

realtime.name: Real-Time Scenario
realtime.description: Processes with strict priority requirements (simulating real-time deadlines)

expectedBehavior.priority-preemptive: Best - ensures high priority processes execute ASAP

teachingPoints: Lower priority tasks may miss deadlines
Fair scheduling not appropriate for real-time

balanced.name: Balanced Workload
balanced.description: Well-balanced mix suitable for general-purpose scheduling comparison
teachingPoints: No single algorithm dominates all metrics

stress.name: Stress Test
stress.description: Many processes to test algorithm performance
teachingPoints: Overhead of complex algorithms more visible

worstcase_fcfs.name: FCFS Worst Case
worstcase_fcfs.description: Longest jobs arrive first - worst case for FCFS

expectedBehavior.sjf: Much better - reverses execution order after P1
expectedBehavior.srtf: Best - quickly preempts for shorter jobs

bestcase_fcfs.name: FCFS Best Case
bestcase_fcfs.description: Shortest jobs arrive first - best case for FCFS

expectedBehavior.fcfs: Performs well - happens to be SJF order
expectedBehavior.sjf: Same result as FCFS for this case

exercises.title: Calculate Metrics Manually
tasks: Calculate completion time for each process
Calculate turnaround time for each process
Calculate waiting time for each process

exercises.title: Compare FCFS and SJF
tasks: Run both algorithms on convoy scenario

exercises.title: Round Robin Quantum Analysis
tasks: Compare context switches and average times

exercises.title: Algorithm Selection
tasks: For each scenario, predict which algorithm will perform best
Analyze why predictions were correct or incorrect
